headline: The US 30 year Treasury yield touched 5.61 percent, its highest since 2002, and the 10 year held a 52 week high of 5.246 percent, sending the S&P 500 to a second straight loss while Nvidia's record 150 billion dollar buyback and Meta's small business Muse launch kept the Nasdaq close to flat.

summary.us: Long-dated Treasuries drove the session on 29 September: the 30 year yield reached 5.61 percent, a level last seen in 2002, on oil-led inflation worry, heavy Treasury issuance and a wave of corporate debt supply, while the 10 year finished at 5.246 percent. The S&P 500 fell 0.16 percent to 7,670.84, the Dow lost 131.59 points to 51,349.92 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.09 percent to 26,797.54, cushioned by Nvidia's 150 billion dollar buyback authorization, a 5 percent bounce in Arm and Meta's Muse for Small Business launch.
summary.india: Nifty 50 closed down 0.28 percent at 22,716.20 and Bank Nifty down 0.39 percent at 54,259.95 on monthly derivatives expiry, with insurance distributors and jewellery names the biggest drags after IRDAI's 23 September consultation paper on commissions and expenses of management. Foreign institutions sold 9,980 crore rupees of cash equities against 6,953 crore rupees of domestic institutional buying, the rupee settled at 95.98 per dollar after a two month low, and the Nifty IT index ended September down 11 percent with Infosys and Wipro at 52 week lows.
summary.global: Asia and Europe both closed mixed on 29 September: the Nikkei 225 fell 0.60 percent to 65,481.27 and the Hang Seng 0.48 percent to 24,523.57, while the DAX added 0.10 percent to 25,399.21 and the FTSE 100 lost 0.45 percent to 10,636.70. Crude gave back the war premium as Saudi Arabia's Yanbu terminal recovered and Hormuz flows reached 13.2 million barrels a day, or 77 percent of prewar levels, taking WTI down 3.06 percent to 89.77 dollars and leaving gold at 4,200.90 dollars and silver at 61.38 dollars after Monday's selloff.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms all week: the US 10 year Treasury yield reached 5.2251 percent on 24 September, its highest since June 2007, and the 30 year touched 5.47 percent, a 22 year high, on strong manufacturing surveys, hawkish Fed commentary and a poorly bid five year auction, which pushed the dollar index to a two month high. Equities absorbed it anyway, because a reported phased US and Iran arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz took WTI down 7.84 percent on the week and because Meta's Muse AI agent kept re-rating the largest index weights, lifting Meta 12.9 percent over five sessions while knocking bank stocks on 23 September as investors weighed whether agents could shop deposit rates on a customer's behalf. India went the other way, undone by a domestic regulator rather than by yields, after the IRDAI consultation paper on insurance distribution economics proposed commission caps and a five year glide path on expenses of management, taking PB Fintech down 33.1 percent on the week and dragging Nifty 50 to a 0.88 percent weekly loss even after Friday's rebound. Precious metals broke their run, with gold off 2.36 percent and silver off 2.77 percent on the week as real yields and the dollar bit, though both recovered on Friday, and copper held a 2.48 percent weekly gain near its 22 September record; crypto diverged from that risk-off tone, with bitcoin adding 3.38 percent and capital rotating into compute and DeFi tokens even after the Bitget hack. Next week the macro calendar is a labour market week rather than an inflation one, with JOLTS on 30 September, ADP and ISM manufacturing on 1 October and jobless claims and factory orders on 2 October, before the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meets 5 to 7 October with the repo rate at 5.25 percent after four pauses.
